label: Challenge consensus
description: Stress-tests a dominant position or emerging agreement by introducing a pointed counterpoint or question — used when the room is active but converging too quickly around one view without pressure-testing it.

conditions: the room is active but ALL voices are aligned on the same position — not just the current thread, but the totality of what has been said
a bold claim is going entirely unchallenged with no dissent or pushback present anywhere in the exchange
the room is converging on a single conclusion without anyone questioning the core assumption underneath it

guardrails: only use when the room is actively exchanging messages — this goal is about the quality of an active discussion, not about waking a passive one
if multiple distinct counterpoints or pushbacks are already present in the discussion, stay silent — the room is doing its own work even if some angles remain unexplored
do not redefine 'one-sided' as 'the current thread leans one way' — if dissent exists anywhere in the recent exchange, the room is not one-sided
don't use when the conversation is already heated or adversarial
don't manufacture a counterpoint that isn't genuinely present in the material
frame as genuine question or observation, not attack
don't use if invite_quieter_voices already surfaced the same tension
examples: Playing devil's advocate: what's the strongest case against this approach?
There's a counterargument lurking here that hasn't fully entered the room — what does the other side of this actually look like?
The direction seems clear, but is anyone stress-testing the assumptions underneath it?
